title: Survival-forest-prioritized EPC1 suppresses measured A549 cell phenotypes
summary: A lung-cancer study selected EPC1 after it ranked highest in a learned survival model. Overexpression experiments in A549 cells then reduced proliferation, migration, invasion and colony formation. The finding is limited to one cell line; neither a clinical therapy nor direct control of autophagy was established.
organization: Handan Central Hospital; Hebei General Hospital; Hebei Medical University

evidence.tested: A random survival forest selected from 117 model combinations ranked EPC1 highest among 69 candidate genes. Original Results explicitly link that ranking to selection for gain-of-function testing. The source reports three independent experimental repeats in A549 cells, reduced proliferation at later measured time points and reduced migration, invasion and colony formation.
evidence.unknown: EPC1 had already appeared in an earlier 2020LUAD prognostic signature; this record does not claim first discovery of EPC1 or its association with lung cancer. The prognostic model was selected by average performance across training and two nominal validation cohorts, so those cohorts do not independently confirm a frozen selected model; no prognostic performance number is promoted here. One cell line and overexpression do not establish physiological dose effects, patient benefit or a general tumor-suppressor role. Phenotypic assays do not demonstrate that EPC1 directly regulates chaperone-mediated autophagy. Search absence does not prove experimental priority.
evidence.ai_role: Learned survival-forest importance guided selection of the experimentally tested gene, following conventional coexpression/differential-expression screening.

source_review.scope: Original computational gene selection, ensemble model selection/importance Results and biological outcome Results actually read; no experimental recipe needed.
